title: Analyzing Student Technology Anxiety in the Context of Digital Transformation in Higher Education: The Role of Personal Characteristics and Self-Efficacy
abstract: In the context of digital transformation in Higher Education, this study aims to examine the role of students’ personal characteristics and self-efficacy in technology use. Although technology is considered a means to enhance teaching and learning, its use in education presents several challenges, including potential technology anxiety among students. To examine this issue, a quantitative study was conducted based on data obtained through a questionnaire administered to 318 undergraduate university students. Data were analyzed through structural equation modeling (SEM). The analysis points to several noteworthy conclusions: (1) specific individual differences, including a proactive personality and psychological capital, predict self-efficacy in the use of technology; (2) the aforementioned characteristics boost students’ self-efficacy; (3) self-efficacy significantly influences technology anxiety, reducing the anxiety associated with technology use; and (4) psychological capital and a more proactive personality indirectly reduce technology anxiety by enhancing self-efficacy. Given these results, personalized interventions tailored to the specific personal characteristics of each student and designed to increase self-efficacy may help reduce students’ anxiety when dealing with technology in educational contexts.
